query: For an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in its uniform, fine lamellar state, whose strength and plasticity remain below industrial application requirements, what single intervention could improve performance for fasteners exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive conditions? State the proposed intervention, mechanism, predicted outcome relative to the starting alloy, applicable operating and test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit falsification criteria.

generation.hypothesis: Thermomechanical processing via heavy cryo-rolling (≈90% reduction) followed by controlled annealing at ~800°C refines the microstructure of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA, thereby providing a significant quantitative improvement—increasing yield strength by at least 30% (target >1500 MPa) and ductility by ~20%—while enhancing creep resistance and corrosion performance in service conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in its as‐cast uniform fine lamellar state.
generation.intervention: Apply heavy cryo-rolling (≈90% thickness reduction) followed by controlled annealing at ~800°C to induce ultrafine recrystallized regions and heterogeneity within the lamellar structure.
generation.conditions: Tested under cyclic thermal conditions up to ~700°C, long-term mechanical loading including room-temperature creep tests, and exposure to chloride-containing corrosive environments simulating fastener service.
generation.structural_mediator: A refined lamellar architecture featuring ultrafine recrystallized FCC regions and partially recovered B2 regions with increased density of phase boundaries acting as crack arresters.
generation.mechanism: Enhanced two-hierarchical constraint and self-generated microcrack arresting mechanisms reduce dislocation mobility and impede grain boundary sliding, thereby increasing yield strength, delaying creep, and limiting corrosive attack.
generation.predicted_outcome: A measurable improvement in yield and ultimate strengths (targeting >1500 MPa yield), increased ductility (at least 20% elongation), and substantially reduced creep rates and corrosion rates compared with the as-cast state.
generation.baseline: The as-cast fine lamellar alloy, which currently exhibits insufficient strength, ductility, creep resistance, and corrosion performance for fastener applications.
generation.boundary: Effectiveness must be maintained up to ~700°C under cyclic thermal and corrosive stresses; industrial scale-up will require precise control of cryo-deformation and annealing parameters to ensure uniform microstructure refinement.
generation.uncertainty: While short-term improvements have been observed in pilot studies, the precise magnitude of long-term improvements under sustained cyclic thermal and corrosive loading remains to be fully validated.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one treated with heavy cryo-rolling and annealing, and one kept in the as-cast state. Subject both sets to tensile tests, creep testing, and accelerated corrosion tests under cyclic thermal conditions up to 700°C.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the treated samples do not exhibit statistically significant improvements (≥30% increase in yield strength and clear reductions in creep and corrosion rates) compared to the as-cast samples under the prescribed conditions, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: In this work, we successfully achieve a superior strength–ductility combination in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEAs by introducing two concurrent effects, the two-hierarchical constraint effect and the self-generated microcrack-arresting mechanisms. The underlying origin lying behind the observed mechanical response is the inherited lamellar geometry from the as-cast EHEA. It is known that grain refinement to the nano/ultrafine-grained regime can render material stronger, but this process is usually accompanied by a dramatic loss of ductility. However, with a composite lamellar architecture, the ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure in this study achieves an improved strength–ductility synergy. Phase decomposition is applied to optimize properties instead of just being a phase-instability phenomenon frequently observed in single-phase HEAs, which may encourage further research in this area. In addition, the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA could be simply processed to achieve properties that are an improvement over traditional TRIP (transformation-induced plasticity) and TWIP (twinning-induced plasticity) steels (Fig. 5). Multiphase materials are evidently suited for tuning their mechanical properties by means of heterostructuring. Recently, the emergence of multicomponent high entropy alloys (HEAs) has opened up the massive composition space for developing alloys with novel microstructures and properties. Eutectic HEAs (EHEAs), first proposed by Lu et al., are a special class of HEAs having promising mechanical properties in the as-cast condition. In particular, the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 nano-lamellar EHEA consisting of soft L12/FCC and hard B2 phases has attracted considerable attention due to their attractive mechanical properties over a wide temperature range, and ample opportunities for further tailoring their microstructure and properties by thermo-mechanical processing (TMP),. Bhattacharjee et al. showed that heavily cryo-rolled and annealed AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA develops a complex heterogeneous microstructure consisting of retained lamellar and coarse non-lamellar regions. The individual domains again consisted of multiscale architecture ranging from ultrafine recrystallized FCC grains to coarse recovered B2 grains, which resulted in simultaneous enhancement in strength and ductility.
